html:
The Hephthalites, sometimes called the White Huns, were a people of Central Asia who built an empire based in Bactria from about 450 to 560. They are one of several Hunnic groups of the period, after the Kidarites and alongside the Alchon Huns.

They were a tribal confederation that included both nomads and town dwellers. From Bactria they ruled east to the Tarim Basin, west into Sogdia and south through Afghanistan. The Hindu Kush roughly marked their limit; the Alchon Huns, once thought to be part of them, held the lands beyond it and raided the Gupta Empire of India.

Their great rival was the Sasanian Empire of Iran:

  • They helped Peroz take the Sasanian throne, then fought him.
  • In 484 they defeated and killed Peroz I, and for years Iran paid them tribute.
  • They backed Kavad I in his struggle for the throne.

Their end came from two sides at once. Around 560 the Türks from the north and the Sasanians under Khosrow I crushed them. Afterwards Hephthalite princes kept small states in Tokharistan under Turkic or Sasanian overlords.

The Buddhas of Bamiyan were carved in the years when they ruled that valley, a sign that Buddhism still thrived in their lands.
